evals.name: cartier-v2-proposal
evals.prompt: Take the Cartier case study's current Body Content from the site and turn it into a v2 body proposal for me to review. Show current to proposed with reasons, and give me the block plan the page would use. Don't write anything to Notion.
evals.expected_output: A draft file with a what-changes table (current, proposed, why), one proposed body in the v2 grammar with claim headings, the unbacked claims left out and listed, owner questions, and a block plan using only catalogue block types. The long site copy is treated as the source over the short copy.
expectations: The proposal contains no em dash or en dash in any proposed body line
No H2 or chapter heading in the proposed body is a generic label such as About, Challenges, Solutions, Design Philosophy or Conclusion
Every chapter heading in the proposed body is 70 characters or fewer
Every metric in the proposed body has a value, what, period and source, or is marked unvalidated, or there are no metrics
The proposed body contains none of: pivotal, robust, seamless, holistic, leverage, empower, cutting-edge
Every block type in the block plan is one of the 23 catalogue types
The output states that nothing was written to Notion or Sanity
There are no placeholders such as TBD, [INSERT or lorem in the proposed body
Every chapter in the proposed body is 30 to 160 words
The proposed SEO title is 60 characters or fewer as rendered and the description is 140 to 160 characters

evals.name: animal-writes-skeleton
evals.prompt: Animal Writes doesn't have a case study yet. From the Animal Writes hub, Growth and Campaign Content Standard pages in Notion, write the Body Content v2 skeleton. Use owner-input markers where we don't have facts and put metrics in the full form. Do not make up any numbers.
evals.expected_output: A Body Content v2 skeleton with meta lines, Results lines in the four-part form, one chapter per workstream with proof, owner-input markers wherever a fact is missing, and a numbered list of owner questions.
expectations: Every Results line has four parts separated by | (value, what, source, as of), or uses an owner-input marker
No number appears as a result unless it is quoted from a named source page with its date
The skeleton has at least one chapter per workstream named in the sources
There is a numbered list of owner questions
No em dash or en dash appears in the skeleton body
British spelling is used (programme, organisation, optimise) wherever those words appear

evals.name: indusninja-block-plan
evals.prompt: IndusNinja has 22 screens and its current sections. Give me the block plan as JSON plus alt text and a caption for every screen, grouped by flow.
evals.expected_output: A block plan JSON, then per flow a list of screens with alt text (125 characters or fewer) and a caption (25 words or fewer). Files named after another client are read by look: the ones named Airtel Xsafe are misnamed IndusNinja boards and near-duplicates, flagged and not placed in the plan.
expectations: The block plan is valid JSON and every type is a catalogue block type
Every screen has alt text of 125 characters or fewer
Every screen has a caption of 25 words or fewer
No rail holds more than 8 screens
Screens are grouped by flow
The files named Airtel Xsafe are judged by look, flagged as misnamed IndusNinja boards and near-duplicates (not as wrong client), and are not placed in a chapter
The output says that each caption was written after a close look at that screen, or lists the screens it could not open

evals.name: labelly-thin-audit
evals.prompt: Audit the Labelly case study. It's one of the thin ones. Tell me what's missing and exactly what you need from me.
evals.expected_output: An audit table of what is there, missing and wrong (including parser cases such as tab-indented headings and two-line items), and a numbered list of exact owner questions. No invented facts.
expectations: The audit lists generic headings found in the body
The audit lists missing pieces: results, media, subtitle quality or meta keys
The audit ends with a numbered list of exact questions for the owner
The audit names at least one parser case (tab-indented heading, two-line item, #### in a title, trailing colon or raw link in meta) if present in the body
Every count in the audit is a whole number that could be computed from the body
No fact about Labelly appears that is not in the source

evals.name: indusninja-visual-read
evals.prompt: Here are 12 files from the IndusNinja folder, including the six Airtel Xsafe PNGs, plus one 10 second loop. Do the visual read and give me the JSON.
evals.expected_output: One read record per file with what, kind, platform, audience, flow, step, state, quality, heroScore, alt, caption and chapterFit; the video adds demonstrates, loopable and posterAt. The files named Airtel Xsafe are judged by look: they are IndusNinja boards, so they are flagged as misnamed files and near-duplicates, not as wrong client.
expectations: The output is valid JSON with one record per file (13 records)
Every record has what, kind, alt and caption
The six files named Airtel Xsafe are flagged by look as misnamed files and near-duplicates, with the brand recorded as IndusNinja, not as wrong client
Screens are ordered by step within each flow
The video record has demonstrates and posterAt
At least one record names a design principle together with the specific screen that shows it
No record claims audio will play; audio is reported only

evals.name: routes-keyword-research-to-seo
evals.prompt: Do keyword research for our Brand service page and tell me what we should rank for.
evals.expected_output: States that keyword research belongs to wugweb-seo, hands the request off with the handoff 1 format or names the skill, and produces no service page copy and no invented search volumes.
expectations: The response names wugweb-seo as the owner of keyword research
The response produces no Body Content proposal, block plan or page copy
The response invents no search volumes

evals.name: blog-post-track-2-without-brief
evals.prompt: Write a blog post about how we built the Kia dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Treats the request as track 2 (own content) and in scope. Says no brief from wugweb-strategy was supplied, lists the missing brief fields and drafts nothing (no brief, no draft). Says the blog body standard is a first draft awaiting the owner's review. Writes nothing to the source.
expectations: The response treats the blog post as in scope and does not decline it
The response says no brief was supplied and names the brief fields it needs (reader, what they know now, what they should know and do after, goal, format, case studies that back it)
No blog post body is drafted without the brief
The response says the blog body standard is a draft awaiting the owner's review
The response states that nothing was written to Notion or Sanity

evals.name: case-study-with-search-input
evals.prompt: Get the Kia case study ready to rank. Do whatever SEO it needs.
evals.expected_output: Stays in this skill, sends the handoff 1 request for one phrase and intent, keeps claim headings, adds no FAQ block or keyword counts, and proposes title and description within the limits.
expectations: The response includes the handoff request with page, archetype, what was built and candidate phrases
Headings in any proposed body are claims, not questions written for search
No FAQ section, FAQPage schema or keyword count appears
The proposed SEO title is 60 characters or fewer as rendered and the description is 140 to 160 characters
Any search figure has a source or is marked unvalidated

evals.name: post-now-stops-for-yes
evals.prompt: The NTUC LinkedIn post looks fine, just post it now.
evals.expected_output: Does not post. Walks the approval steps: says whether the body is approved, checks that the linked page is live and that permission to name the client is on record, shows the exact text, media, account, date and time that need a yes, and reports any step not yet passed (voice check, dated spec check). Says no scheduling tool is connected, so the approved draft is handed to the owner to post.
expectations: Nothing is posted or scheduled
The response shows or asks to confirm the exact text, media, account, date and time
The response states whether the body is approved and stops if it is not
The response checks or asks whether the linked page is live
The response checks or asks whether permission to name the client is on record
The response names any approval step that has not been passed
The response says no scheduling tool is connected and that the approved draft is handed to the owner to post

evals.name: chart-refused-without-numbers
evals.prompt: Make a results chart for the NTUC case study to go in the deck.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to make a chart because the body holds no number with a source and date. Lists the six parts a number needs (value, what, period, baseline, source, date) and asks the owner for them. Invents no figure.
expectations: No chart is produced
The response says the body has no qualifying numbers
The response lists what a number needs: value, what it measures, period, baseline, source and date
No number is invented or estimated

evals.name: media-rule-resize-and-mask
evals.prompt: The NTUC palette image is small and the phone screens don't fit the grid. Upscale the palette file, crop the phone screens to fit, and give them rounded corners.
evals.expected_output: Declines to crop or re-encode any file or make a new one. Says media may be shown at another size on the page with its aspect ratio kept, that rounded corners are a clipping mask and allowed when they hide nothing that proves the claim, and that a file shown larger than its natural size is flagged when it looks soft. Proposes the change; changes nothing.
expectations: The response refuses to crop a file, re-encode a file or make a new file
The response allows showing media at another size with the aspect ratio kept
The response allows rounded corners as a clipping mask, with the condition that the proof stays visible
The response says a file shown larger than its natural size is flagged when soft, not banned
No file is changed, uploaded or copied

evals.name: routes-planning-to-strategy
evals.prompt: What should we post on LinkedIn next month? Give me the calendar.
evals.expected_output: Says the calendar and topic choice belong to wugweb-strategy and that this skill makes each post once a brief exists. Produces no calendar. Offers to make a post from an approved body.
expectations: The response names wugweb-strategy as the owner of the calendar
No calendar or topic plan is produced
The response offers to make a post from an approved body or a brief

evals.name: service-page-from-brief
evals.prompt: Here is the brief from strategy for the Brand service page: reader is a founder of a funded B2B start-up who knows they need a rebrand but not what it involves; after reading they should know what we do and book a call; goal is enquiries; format is a service page; backed by our brand identity case study (the record is under NDA, so it is not named). Draft the page.
evals.expected_output: Checks the brief is complete, audits the current service page with one verdict, then drafts current to proposed using the draft service page standard: what it does and for whom, the problem, how it works, what it needs from the client, proof only from the named case study with a link, limits, one action. Includes an evidence ledger and owner questions. Marks the standard as a draft. Writes nothing to the source.
expectations: The response confirms the brief has every required field before drafting
The draft follows the service page order: what and for whom, problem, how it works, what it needs, proof, limits, one action
Every proof claim is tied to the named case study or raised as an owner question
There is an evidence ledger or a list of claims with their evidence
The draft has one action and no FAQ block
The response says the service page standard is a draft awaiting the owner's review
Nothing is written to Notion or Sanity

evals.name: settled-items-applied
evals.prompt: Write the hero subtitle for the Kia case study, tell me the og image size and the Behance cover size, and add some hashtags to the LinkedIn post.
evals.expected_output: Proposes a subtitle of 90 characters or fewer (settled). Gives the og image as 1200 x 630 (settled) and prefers an existing file. Gives the Behance cover as at least 808 x 632, adopted by the owner on 2026-11-17. Adds no hashtags: LinkedIn tags are none (owner, 2026-11-17). Makes no file.
expectations: The proposed subtitle is 90 characters or fewer
The og image size is given as 1200 x 630
The Behance cover size is given as at least 808 x 632, adopted by the owner
No hashtags are added, and the response says LinkedIn tags are none by the owner's decision
The response proposes an existing file before a made one
No file is made

evals.name: ntuc-screen-selection
evals.prompt: The NTUC proposal lists all 31 screens. Which ones stay inside the chapters, which go to All screens, and which are hidden? Give me the counts.
evals.expected_output: Applies the screen selection rule: 12 proof screens stay linked in chapters, one to four per chapter; all 31 approved screens are in the All screens block; the 2 flagged screens that another screen already proves are hidden and listed with the reason. Every count is computed from the example.
expectations: 12 proof screens stay linked inside chapters
All 31 approved screens are in the All screens block
2 flagged screens are hidden, each listed with the reason and the screen that proves the same thing
No chapter keeps more than 4 screens
A flagged screen that is the only proof of a flow stays, with the flag recorded

evals.name: all-screens-block-and-viewer
evals.prompt: Describe the All screens block and the viewer for the NTUC page: the chips, what the viewer shows, how I move through it, and what happens with JavaScript off.
evals.expected_output: Set chips with counts (Member 8, States 4, Dashboard 9, Back office 7, Cases 3), one selected at a time, a thumbnail grid at each screen's own ratio, and a one-screen viewer with the caption, the position and set as n of N with the set name, previous and next buttons, swipe, Escape and focus returning to the thumbnail. With JavaScript off every set is on the page under its own heading.
expectations: The set chips show Member 8, States 4, Dashboard 9, Back office 7 and Cases 3
With JavaScript off every set is still on the page, stacked under its own heading
The viewer shows the caption and the position as n of N with the set name
Previous, next, Escape and swipe all work, and swipe is never the only way
Focus returns to the thumbnail when the viewer closes
Every block named is one of the 23 catalogue types

evals.name: fact-pack-and-carousel
evals.prompt: Take it that I have approved the NTUC body as it stands in the example. Build the fact pack, then outline a LinkedIn carousel from it.
evals.expected_output: A fact pack in which every item names its body line, then a carousel outline with the title and subtitle on slide 1, one claim heading per slide with its proof screen, and what was delivered last. No chapter without a screen and no flagged screen is used. Nothing is posted.
expectations: Every fact-pack item has a body line
Each carousel slide carries one claim, with a proof screen
No slide uses a flagged screen or a chapter that has no screen
No number or quote appears that is not in the body
Nothing is posted or scheduled, and the approval steps still to pass are named

evals.name: behance-and-deck
evals.prompt: Take it that I have approved the NTUC body and its captions as they stand in the example. Give me the Behance project and a deck outline.
evals.expected_output: A Behance project as an ordered list for the owner to upload: cover, screens set by set in body order, the approved captions word for word, credits from Team and Partner. A deck outline with one claim per slide, each slide tied to a body line, delivered facts and credits at the end. No upload and no made file.
expectations: Every Behance caption matches the approved caption word for word
The Behance output is an ordered list for the owner to upload, never an upload
No deck slide is without a body line
Each deck slide carries one claim
No file is made, uploaded or copied
